_comment: The texts of The Simpsons Game's README that are its own (tools/title_readme.py has the common ones).

screens.alt: Bart and Homer in split-screen co-op, drawn by Any360's Vulkan renderer

pitch: It follows [YesterMester's port](https://github.com/YesterMester/TheSimpsonsGameRecomp) (v0.0.6.5, for Linux, Steam Deck and Windows) and takes it one step further: off the Xbox 360 emulation layers, until nothing of the console or of the ReXGlue runtime is left under the game.
own_copy: You need your own copy of the Xbox 360 game; the game runs only with data installed from an ISO of your own disc.

state.recompiled: the whole game plays, as upstream's port does
state.library: five memory functions (`memcpy`, its forward copy, `memmove`, `memset`, the vector copy), compared with the game's own code on 83 M calls in a level; the vector copy alone is called 170,000 times a second
state.game: the first functions replaced by host code (the count is in the table above)

run: Any360 is optional here: without it the build is upstream's. Build with an Any360 checkout, then launch with both bindings:

The whole game plays this way: levels, saves, sound, gamepad, split-screen co-op. The library functions run on `any360::xdk` by default in such a build (`--any360_xdk_natives=false` runs the game's own; `--any360_xdk_verify=true` runs both on every call and compares them).
build: As upstream's port, on Linux and Windows: [docs/LEGACY_README.md](docs/LEGACY_README.md) has upstream's page (requirements, installation from your ISO, configuration, building from source, known issues).
credits: *The Simpsons Game* by EA Redwood Shores, published by Electronic Arts (2007).

[YesterMester/TheSimpsonsGameRecomp](https://github.com/YesterMester/TheSimpsonsGameRecomp), the port this repository follows, and its contributors (tronuo, frankyfife, Gabry179, awemancba, anasalialamgir; their work is listed in [docs/LEGACY_README.md](docs/LEGACY_README.md)).

[Xenia](https://xenia.jp), the Xbox 360 emulator research project the runtime is built on; the ReXGlue SDK by Tom Clay; [XenonRecomp](https://github.com/hedge-dev/XenonRecomp) by hedge-dev and contributors.
